newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila upholds life term on Briton in drugs case.
newsitem.headline: Manila upholds life term on Briton in drugs case.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Thursday affirmed a life term imposed by a judge on a British national for allegedly attempting to transport 5.6 kg (12.3 lb) of hashish to Australia in 1992.
The accused, William Burton, had asked the Supreme Court to void the judge's verdict on grounds he did not know the bags he checked in at the Manila airport on his way to Sydney contained the drugs.

Burton testified in his trial he bought the bags, as well as the pair of shoes he was wearing, from an acquaintance without knowing they concealed the hashish. Agents also found drugs in the shoes, according to court records.
The Supreme Court said Burton's contention that he did not know he had the drugs in his possession was uncorroborated and insufficient to overturn the original verdict.

"Under the facts obtaining in this case, the 5.6 kilos of hashish cleverly and painstakingly concealed inside appellant's luggage and rubber shoes can be said to be in the possession and control of appellant with his knowledge," it said.

The Supreme Court on February 10 also affirmed the conviction by a trial judge of another Briton, Nigel Richard Gatward, on charges of heroin smuggling. But instead of the 35 years in jail imposed by the judge on Gatward, the court raised the jail sentence to 40 years.
